newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Bank denies report Kopper criticised Kohl.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bank denies report Kopper criticised Kohl.

text.p: Deutsche Bank sharply rebuffed on Sunday a German newspaper report alleging the bank's chairman, Hilmar Kopper, had slammed Bonn government policies, saying few details in the article were correct.
Berlin-based Welt am Sonntag published a front-page story which said Kopper had expressed "massive criticism" about Chancellor Helmut Kohl's economic policies.

The newspaper said it had based the article on information received from unnamed sources present at a meeting held on January 29 between Kopper and members of Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) sister party.

"Apart from the time and the date of a meeting between Mr. Kopper and (CDU/CSU) parliamentarians, nothing is correct in the article," Deutsche Bank spokesman Hellmut Hartmann told Reuters in answer to a query.
In a letter to the editor, obtained by Reuters, Hartmann said he was surprised the newspaper had based an article on unverified comments and asked him to issue a correction.

Hartmann said the meeting had focused on Europe's planned single currency and Germany's position as a financial centre and that "comments attributed to Mr Kopper and pertaining to other topics were the opposite of what was actually said".
"How (Kopper's) praise for the ruling coalition's reform plans could be transformed into massive criticism is incomprehensible to me," he said.

The newspaper said Kopper criticised Bonn for a lack of innovation in making the economy more flexible and that he was concerned about Bonn's plans to cut public spending. Kopper suggested high transfer payments to east German states needed to be cut, the paper reported.
According to the paper, Kopper was concerned about Italy's plans to join Europe's currency union from the start in 1999 since Italy has been known for its inflationary policies.

One of the parliamentarians who met Kopper also said the article was misleading. Gunnar Uldall, economic spokesman for Kohl's CDU, told Reuters: "The impression the article is trying to create is definitely false."
Although some critical comments were made during the long meeting, Uldall said Kopper had suggested Kohl's government was pursuing the right policies on the whole.
Uldall said none of the participants had left the meeting feeling that "the government had been dealt a real beating."
